newsitem.title: USA: Ban on gifts to Illinois officials proposed.
newsitem.headline: Ban on gifts to Illinois officials proposed.

text.p: An Illinois lawmaker unveiled on Monday legislation that would prohibit state constitutional officers, legislators and their staffs from accepting gifts from lobbyists.
State Rep. Jan Schakowsky, D-Evanston, said she proposed the ban as part of a legislative package she introduced late last week in the Illinois General Assembly.
The ban would extend to gifts, meals, services, lodging, tickets to events and other things of value, according to Schakowsky.
In addition to constitutional officers and legislators, the ban would also include state appointees, such as members of state agencies, she said.

Schakowsky said her proposal would go farther than a 1993 law that required persons lobbying for state contracts to register with the secretary of state's office and disclose any expenditure made to acquire the contract, including gifts.

Since that time, dozens of securities firms vying for state bond business registered their bankers or lobbyists to comply with the law and several firms reported thousands of dollars in expenditures on state officials.
"In my view, the gift sets off a sense of reciprocity," Schakowsky said.

In addition to the gift ban, Schakowsky's legislative package also calls for prohibiting political contributions from the utility and gaming industries and a voluntary limit on campaign expenditures with campaign funding coming from a publicly financed "clean elections fund."
Schakowsky said she was optimistic about the legislation's chances for passage given recent attention to campaign financing on the national level.
